title: Geographic access request: eligibility checklist and safe-failover policy
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Purpose: define a deterministic intake and eligibility flow for customer requests related to region availability and data residency constraints, plus a documented safe-failover policy when exact residency cannot be immediately satisfied. Goal is to reduce ad-hoc decisions, accelerate response SLA for enterprise customers, and provide clear handoffs to engineering, legal, and operations. This ticket captures the proposed checklist, scoring guidelines, required engineering and compliance gates, and a canned customer communication template.

Scope: non-bug requests from sales or customer success asking for new regions, strict residency (data must not leave country X), DR failover regions, or tenancy preferences. Not in scope: underlying infra procurement (cloud contracts) or detailed network design which will be handed to ENG-ops workstreams.

High-level flow: intake form -> automated eligibility checks (capacity, model availability, regulatory blacklist) -> PM scoring (customer risk, revenue, feasibility) -> engineering impact analysis (infra, CI/CD, rollout) -> legal/compliance clearance -> pilot & canary -> full onboarding.

Outputs: 1) Eligibility checklist and scoring sheet 2) Safe-failover policy (what fallback regions we will offer and messaging) 3) Triage SLA (48h initial response, 10 business days formal feasibility note) 4) Customer response templates and internal handoff checklist.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form mapped to automated checks and generates a scorecard
Scoring thresholds with explicit outcomes (Accept / Needs follow-up / Decline)
List of required engineering gates with owners and estimated ETA
Safe-failover policy documented with allowed fallback regions per residency tier
Standard reply templates for Sales/CS with next steps and estimated timelines
Escalation path to Legal/Compliance and Sales Ops included

owner_notes: We must keep canned messaging for Sales predictable—avoid promising timelines until infra verification is complete. For strict residency asks, prioritize Dedicated/private offers and surface cost uplift early. Consider building a simple automaton that rejects requests where model availability or legal restrictions are absolute blockers.
customer_template: Thanks for your request. We received your region/data residency inquiry and will respond within 48 hours with an initial feasibility summary. Next steps typically include: (1) confirmation of strict residency requirements, (2) internal legal and infra review, (3) pilot provisioning or contract exception path. Estimated feasibility window: 10 business days. If the requirement is strict residency for regulated data, we will likely propose Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) and share cost estimates.
